name: Mike Johnson
current_role: Speaker of the U.S. House and U.S. Representative for LA-4
bio: Mike Johnson has represented Louisiana's 4th District since 2017 and became the 56th Speaker of the House in 2023. He previously served in the Louisiana House of Representatives and chaired the Republican Study Committee. Before elected office he was a constitutional lawyer, including with Alliance Defending Freedom; he is from Shreveport.

platform.point: Calls for balancing the federal budget, reforming entitlement programs and cutting wasteful spending to address the national debt.
Supports a peace-through-strength approach built on military superiority to deter aggression.
Backs protecting unborn life and honoring marriage and family as core institutions.
Campaigns on lowering costs and expanding American energy production.
Favors limited federal government and free-market policies as core principles.

economy.evidence: Supports tax cuts and opposed a $15 federal minimum wage; official site calls for spending cuts and tax reform.

welfare.evidence: Has backed repealing the Affordable Care Act and calls for entitlement reform.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion restrictions and has backed bills limiting LGBTQ rights; abortion weighed most.

security.evidence: Opposed adding a warrant requirement to FISA Section 702 surveillance and backed National Guard use during 2025 Los Angeles protests.

immigration.evidence: Has pushed legislation limiting asylum and tightening border enforcement.

foreign.evidence: Brought military aid for Ukraine and Israel to a House vote and promotes peace through strength.

energy.evidence: Promotes American energy dominance and has opposed climate regulations.

faith.evidence: Official site says a just government embraces the cultural influence of religion and morality.

notes: Tech and education left null: no clear recorded evidence found in the sources reviewed.

name: Mike Nichols
bio: Mike Nichols is a biologist from Pitkin, Louisiana. He is running as a Republican in the 4th District against incumbent Speaker Mike Johnson.
notes: Campaign site lists no issue positions or biography; background is from the Wikipedia race article and Louisiana Radio Network.

name: Conrad Cable
bio: Conrad Cable is a farmer from Farmerville in north Louisiana. He is running as a Democrat for the 4th District, campaigning on agriculture, health care and worker issues.

platform.point: Supports Medicare for All and opposes federal cuts to Medicaid.
Wants higher wages and stronger protections for union organizing.
Proposes public grocery stores in rural and low-income areas stocked with local food and accepting SNAP and WIC.
Backs overturning Citizens United and banning stock trading by members of Congress.
Argues current farm and trade policy has hurt Louisiana soybean growers.

economy.evidence: Calls for higher wages, union protections and publicly run grocery stores.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and opposes Medicaid cuts.

notes: Social handles are listed as @conrad4congress on the campaign site; exact profile URLs were not individually verified. Sources differ on whether he is a first- or fifth-generation farmer.

name: Matt Gromlich
bio: Matt Gromlich is a longtime educator who teaches at LSU Shreveport. He is from the Shreveport area and lives in Greenwood. He is running as a Democrat for the 4th District.

platform.point: Supports health care that is free at the point of service and federal oversight of drug prices.
Backs raising the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour with support for small employers.
Would lift the payroll tax cap on high earners to shore up Social Security.
Proposes child care subsidies, universal pre-K, higher teacher pay and more career and technical education.
Calls for pausing data center projects until community safety is assured and requiring transparency on industrial deals.
Supports overturning Citizens United, congressional term limits and a ban on stock trading by members.

economy.evidence: Backs a $15 minimum wage, federal drug price oversight and lifting the payroll tax cap for high earners.

welfare.evidence: Supports health care free at the point of service, universal pre-K and child care subsidies.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and gender-affirming care, and backs gun rights with added safeguards.

immigration.evidence: Pairs border security with calls for faster, more affordable legal immigration.

foreign.evidence: Favors strong alliances and diplomacy while opposing open-ended military interventions.

tech.evidence: Opposes unregulated tech development and calls for a data center moratorium pending safety guarantees.

education.evidence: Calls for higher teacher pay, universal pre-K and investment in public education.

notes: Energy left null: he opposes carbon capture projects and data centers, which does not map clearly onto the scale.

name: Michael Echols
current_role: Louisiana State Representative (District 14) and House Majority Leader
bio: Michael Echols has represented District 14 in the Louisiana House since 2020 and became House Republican Majority Leader in December 2025. He previously served on the Monroe City Council, including as chair. Born in Bastrop, he lives in Monroe and has worked in development, construction, health care, real estate and insurance.

platform.point: Pledges to secure the border and stop illegal immigration.
Says he will protect farmers and rural communities.
Focuses on hospital accountability, transparency and rural health care access.
Promotes reducing regulatory burdens on small businesses.
Aims to make everyday life more affordable and strengthen the economy.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on cutting regulatory burdens for small businesses and received an NFIB small-business award.

immigration.evidence: Pledges to seal the border and cut off illegal immigration.

name: Stewart Cathey Jr.
bio: Stewart Cathey Jr. has served in the Louisiana Senate since 2020 and chairs its agriculture and rural development committee. He is a U.S. Army engineer officer who deployed twice to Afghanistan, and he runs a management consulting firm. He was born in Monroe and graduated from the University of Louisiana at Monroe.

platform.point: Describes education as the foundation of a prosperous community.
Says he will bring a commonsense approach to the region's challenges.

notes: He entered the race on July 8, 2026; his campaign site gives little issue detail. Ballotpedia could not be retrieved.

name: Gabe Firment
bio: Gabe Firment has represented District 22 in the Louisiana House since 2020 and chairs its Insurance Committee. He has worked in construction and insurance and owns a small business. He grew up in Rapides Parish and lives in Grant Parish.

platform.point: Pledges to protect national sovereignty and enforce immigration law.
Wants to expand American energy production to create jobs and lower costs.
Says he will protect Social Security and Medicare for future generations.
Supports the farm economy, timber jobs and rural communities.
Pledges to defend gun rights.

economy.evidence: Lists lower taxes as a core value.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: describes himself as pro-life; guns: pledges to defend Second Amendment rights; no other issues addressed on his campaign site.

immigration.evidence: Campaigns on border security and enforcing immigration law.

energy.evidence: Calls for expanding American energy production to lower costs.

notes: Liberty lowered from 85 to 65 after an unverified claim about a transgender care bill was removed; the score now rests on his pro-life and pro-gun statements.

name: Pat Moore
bio: Patricia "Pat" Moore has represented District 17 in the Louisiana House since 2019. She previously served on the Ouachita Parish Police Jury from 2007 to 2019 and retired from State Farm. She is from Monroe and graduated from the University of Louisiana at Monroe.

platform.point: Aims to lower everyday costs, support fair wages and make child care affordable.
Wants to protect rural hospitals, lower medicine costs and expand behavioral health care.
Supports good schools and help for teachers across the district.
Seeks infrastructure investment for every parish plus workforce training and small-business support.
Pledges to stay accessible to constituents and work across party lines.

welfare.evidence: Campaigns on affordable child care and lower health care costs, including for seniors.

liberty.evidence: In 2024 voted in committee to advance a bill removing obscenity-law protections for teachers and librarians; speech was the issue.

education.evidence: Emphasizes public school quality and support for teachers.

notes: The liberty score rests on a single committee vote; campaign headshot is hosted on GitHub rather than the campaign domain.

name: Misti Cordell
current_role: Chair of the Louisiana Board of Regents
bio: Misti Cordell chairs the Louisiana Board of Regents and has held roles in Governor Jeff Landry's administration. She is a health care consultant and business owner who has advocated for rural communities and independent physicians. Her campaign is based in West Monroe.

platform.point: Pledges to secure the border, finish the wall and take on drug cartels.
Wants tax cuts so families keep more of their earnings.
Favors market-based steps to expand doctor access and patient choice over federal mandates.
Supports school choice and less federal control of education.
Pledges to protect Louisiana's energy industry by cutting regulations.
Backs anti-abortion policies, gun rights, religious freedom and limits on transgender athletes in women's sports.

economy.evidence: Calls for tax cuts and reduced federal regulation.

welfare.evidence: Prefers market-based health care solutions over federal mandates.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion restrictions, gun rights and limits on transgender athletes in women's sports.

immigration.evidence: Calls for finishing the border wall and stopping illegal immigration.

energy.evidence: Pledges to cut regulations affecting Louisiana's energy industry.

education.evidence: Supports school choice and opposes federal control of schools.

faith.evidence: Pledges to defend religious freedom and traditional values.

notes: Ballotpedia could not be retrieved to confirm further biographical details.

name: Austin Magee
current_role: Owner of an industrial welding and mechanical company
bio: Austin Magee owns Pittman Industrial, a welding and mechanical contracting company that works across Louisiana. He was born and raised in the 5th District and attended high school and college there. He has not previously held elected office.

platform.point: Says he will resist government overreach that erodes individual freedoms.
Presents his work experience as a basis for practical, common-sense representation.

notes: Campaign site gives no specific policy positions; the headshot URL is an image on the homepage and may not be a formal portrait.

name: Oscar Dantzler
current_role: Former police officer and bail bondsman
bio: Oscar "Omar" Dantzler is a former police officer and bail bondsman. He ran for the 5th District as a Democrat in 2022 and for governor in 2019, and is running as a Republican in 2026.
notes: No campaign website or issue statements found; background is from the Wikipedia race article.

name: Dan McKay
bio: Dan McKay is an attorney running as a Democrat for the 5th District. His campaign describes him as a veteran, former prosecutor and country lawyer.
notes: Campaign homepage lists no policy positions and its about page was unavailable; the campaign image may be a graphic rather than a headshot.
